subject: Genetics
title: Copy Number Surprises
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Copy Number Surprises.

hook.text: You might have 2 copies of a gene. Your neighbor might have 14. Copy number variation was a total surprise.

buildup.text: The genome project assumed everyone had two copies of each gene. Post-project studies found massive variation.

discovery.text: Copy number variants cover 4.8% of the genome—more DNA variation than single-letter changes. Size matters.

twist.text: AMY1 gene copies vary from 2 to 15. More copies mean more amylase enzyme—better starch digestion. Diet shaped genes.

climax.text: CNVs explain disease risks that single mutations can't. Schizophrenia, autism, and HIV resistance all involve CNVs.

punchline.text: It's not just which genes you have. It's how many copies.

quiz.question: What are copy number variants?
options: Different numbers of gene copies between people
